headline: Palladian's Clean Air Scam: Poor Districts Breathed Poison by Design
body:
A cache of internal Palladian communications obtained by the Lake Monitor reveals that the corponation's atmospheric processing division deliberately throttled air filtration output in the Gray Zone and The Narrows for a period of at least six years, beginning in 2174. The documents show that Palladian engineers were directed by senior management to run processing units in low-income districts at 40-60% of rated capacity while billing the Meridian municipal authority for full operation — a scheme that netted an estimated 220 million quanta in fraudulent service fees while exposing roughly 900,000 residents to particulate and toxin levels two to four times the legal threshold. Internal messaging reviewed by this outlet includes a 2176 note from regional operations director Henryk Vassiliev-Crane describing the throttling as 'load optimization in low-priority zones.'

The health impact is staggering. Respiratory disease rates in the Gray Zone have been climbing at 11% annually since 2174 — a trend that district health clinics flagged repeatedly to Meridian's environmental authority, which is itself a partial Palladian contract recipient. 'We were telling anyone who would listen that something was wrong with the air,' said Clinic Director Amara Oyelaran-Beck, who runs a community health center in the Gray Zone's lower tier. 'The data was there. Nobody looked because nobody wanted to look.' Palladian's board has placed Vassiliev-Crane on administrative leave and issued a statement calling the documents 'selectively contextualized.'

The Collective has filed a class-action claim on behalf of 340 named plaintiffs and is seeking 1.4 billion quanta in damages. The Underground Signal is reporting that at least two of the engineers who signed off on the throttling directives have already left GLMZ — one to a Palladian facility in the northern corridor, one to a destination that Federal Remnant border records show as unlogged.
aftermath: Palladian settled the class-action for 180 million quanta — 22% of their estimated fraudulent gain — with a non-disclosure clause attached; Vassiliev-Crane resurfaced eighteen months later as a consultant for Arcturus Defense's facilities management division.
runner_relevance: The scandal opened several high-paying runner contract streams: The Collective and independent attorneys hired data-retrieval runners to pull additional Palladian documentation from secure servers before the corponation's legal team could sanitize them; rival corponations — notably Axiom — contracted intelligence runners to assess whether the scandal created an acquisition opportunity for Palladian's atmospheric processing contracts; bounty-style contracts emerged for locating the two fled engineers before they could be permanently relocated beyond reach; and protection runners were hired to guard Collective attorneys and key plaintiffs who began receiving credible threats shortly after the lawsuit was filed.
